claims.statement: G subset-of G' implies A_G(Delta) subset-of A_G'(Delta).
Over-approximation is sound, and the extra work equals |A_G'(Delta) minus A_G*(Delta)|, every element reachable from the head of an added edge.
Under-approximation's wrongly-retained set is exactly A_G*(Delta) minus A_G''(Delta), equivalently the nodes whose every true path from Delta uses a missing edge.
For every nonnegative weighting, the minimum-weight sound set is A_G*(Delta) itself.
Inclusion orders cost and safety oppositely; G* is the unique point optimal in both.

enumeration.graphs: all DAGs on n nodes for n in 3..5 under a fixed topological order, so every subset of the allowed edge set is a DAG
enumeration.over_approximations: every superset of G* within the allowed edge set
enumeration.weightings: a frozen family of nonnegative weightings including uniform, head-heavy, tail-heavy and a zero weighting

controls.statement: A planted under-approximation that genuinely misses a reachable node must be reported unsound by the SAME predicate used for real cases. Without this, 'no unsound over-approximation found' is indistinguishable from a predicate that cannot fire.
N3 is checked as SET EQUALITY against an independently computed wrongly-retained set, not as containment in one direction.
Under the all-zero weighting every sound set ties at weight 0; N4 must still report A_G*(Delta) as A minimum and must NOT report a violation. A checker that alarms here is wrong about its own claim.

The sweep must contain at least one strict over-approximation with positive extra work and at least one strict under-approximation with a nonempty wrongly-retained set, or the theorems are being verified only on degenerate inputs.

conditions: N1 to N5 hold with no counterexample
terminals.licenses: A bounded statement that graph quality, not weighting, determines revalidation cost and safety: over-approximation is sound at an exactly characterised price, under-approximation fails exactly on nodes whose every path uses a missing edge, and no nonnegative weighting improves on the affected closure.
does_not_license: any claim that real extraction yields G*

conditions: N1 or N2 has a counterexample
N3's set equality fails, or some nonnegative weighting beats A_G*(Delta)
terminals.reading: The cost account is wrong; savings would then depend on weighting after all.

real_system_evidence.consequence: NO FROZEN TEST IS RUN AGAINST IT. Its numbers were read before this theory was authored, so any reference is a labelled retrospective consistency observation and evidences nothing.
real_system_evidence.why: Python import graphs are a superset of true semantic dependencies, so they instantiate the over-approximation case of N2 and cannot certify G* itself.

stop_rule: Outcomes are read once. On T2 or T3 the law is refuted and the lane stops. On T1 the theorem stands but, because extraction is not authoritative for G*, #1649's stop rule keeps ORION-16 in the bounded lane and forbids any deployed-system claim.
